titleEn: In the Box by the Sacks—Pop!

pages.text: "Pebbles and flute, let's play!" Little brother Mumu tipped pebbles onto the mill floor. Pebbles rolled, and the straw flute tumbled. Marks dotted the floury floor. Spilling was fun; picking up wasn't.
Dad from the mill came in carrying a wheat sack. "Mumu, watch your feet—oh dear!" He stepped on a pebble and wobbled. The sack tipped, spilling flour.
Mumu hurried to find his straw flute. But it was gone! He looked under sacks and rummaged in the flour. "Where's my flute?" Tears filled his eyes.
Dad set down the sack and crouched beside him. "Want to learn a magic trick?" Dad tapped an empty box by the sacks. Big sister Dodo slipped through the door to watch.
Dad stretched a wing toward the floury floor. "Without tidying, this happens." Dad's foot hurt, the sack wobbled, and the flute hid away. "This mill is hurting!" Mumu pouted his beak.
"But tidy up..." Dad tapped his wing on top of the box. "No sore foot, a steady sack, and pop—the flute appears! That's pop magic." Mumu stretched his neck toward the box, eager to try.
Dad sang, "Pebbles with pebbles, in the box by the sacks—pop!" Mumu gathered pebbles in both wings and rolled them into the box. Pop! Dodo picked up one too. Pop! "In the box by the sacks—pop!"
The last pebble went into the box. Pop! The floury floor was smooth again. Dad lifted his sack and strode past. Mumu flicked his tail once. "Now the mill doesn't hurt!"
Then the straw flute appeared behind the box! "My flute!" Mumu hugged it with both wings. "One, gather things that belong together! Two, in the box by the sacks—pop! Three, all done, feeling lively!"
Dad tucked Mumu inside his wings. "Our tidying champion!" Tidying makes feet, sacks, and hearts feel lively. With the flute held in a wing, Mumu called, "In the box by the sacks—pop!"
